classes.NOUN.mass: mass nouns used without a plural in everyday Hebrew (שׁוּם, בְּרוֹקוֹלִי, תִּירָס …)
classes.VERB.copula: הָיָה “to be”: no present tense in use, so past, future and infinitive cells
classes.PRON.dem: the demonstrative זֶה / זֹאת / אֵלֶּה, alone (presenting) and with the article after a definite noun (הַזֶּה / הַזֹּאת / הָאֵלֶּה)
classes.ADP.suffixed: a prefix preposition (לְ) whose pronoun forms are separate words (לִי, לְךָ …)
classes.DET.dem: the distal demonstrative הַהוּא / הַהִיא / הָהֵם / הָהֵן “that, those”, after a definite noun
classes.NOUN.plt: nouns used only in the plural (אֲנָשִׁים “people”)
classes.NOUN.sgt: count nouns with no plural in use (אָדָם “person”: the plural is said with another word, אֲנָשִׁים / בְּנֵי אָדָם)
classes.NUM.gender: a number with a masculine and a feminine form (1, 11–19): אֶחָד / אַחַת, אַחַד עָשָׂר / אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה
classes.NUM.two: two: masculine and feminine, alone (שְׁנַיִם / שְׁתַּיִם) and in the construct form used before a noun (שְׁנֵי / שְׁתֵּי)
classes.NUM.const: 3–10: the masculine form (in -ָה, with masculine nouns), the feminine form, and the masculine construct used before a definite noun (שְׁלוֹשֶׁת הַ…)
classes.NUM.dual: hundred and thousand: one (מֵאָה, אֶלֶף), two as a dual (מָאתַיִם, אַלְפַּיִם) and the plural used from three on (שְׁלוֹשׁ מֵאוֹת, שְׁלוֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים)
classes.PRON.all: כֹּל “all” with a personal ending: כֻּלָּנוּ “all of us”, כֻּלְּכֶם / כֻּלְּכֶן “all of you”, כֻּלָּם / כֻּלָּן “all of them, everyone”
classes.DET.int: the interrogative אֵיזֶה “which?”: אֵיזֶה (m.), אֵיזוֹ (f.), אֵילוּ (plural), before the noun
classes.NOUN.cal: names of the weekdays and months (יוֹם שֵׁנִי, מַאי): used as names — without the article and, in everyday use, without a plural; “on Monday” = בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי, “in May” = בְּמַאי
classes.ADJ.inv: an invariable adjective-like word with one form for every gender and number (בְּסֵדֶר “fine, OK”); ordinary adjectives (class-less ADJ) have eight cells: masculine / feminine × singular / plural, without and with the article
